compiled:
📰 General

Macklemore Claims Arenas Declined Free Palestine Tour, Sparking Outrage •

Macklemore announced plans for a benefit tour, the “Free Palestine Tour,” featuring shows in Dublin, London, and Paris. Following the initial announcement, Macklemore stated that several U.S. arenas declined to host dates for the tour. He alleges that these venues, mirroring the behavior of football stadiums, rejected the opportunity to support the initiative. The tour proceeded with shows outside of the United States, raising questions about the reasons behind the U.S. arenas’ decisions.

🌍 World

Strong Earthquake Shakes Japanese Coast Near Tokyo, No Tsunami Warning Issued •

A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Japan near Hasaki, approximately 155 miles east of Tokyo. The quake occurred at 7:30 p.m. local time and was detected by seismic monitoring stations. Authorities have confirmed that no tsunami warning has been issued following the event. Initial reports indicate the quake caused shaking felt in the region, but no immediate damage has been reported.

🦅 US

Pinkins Campaigning in Mississippi Senate Race, Aiming to Disrupt Republican Frontrunners •

Ty Pinkins, a longshot candidate in Mississippi’s Senate race, stated his initial intention was to disrupt the Republican primary. Following an April poll indicating a lack of competitive chances, Pinkins remained in the race. He intends to spoil the results of the primary election. Pinkins’ strategy focuses on challenging the established candidates, Colom and Hyde-Smith, within the Democratic primary.

💰 Business

Retail Traders Initiate Massive Stock Sell-Off, Largest Since 2020 •

Retail investors executed a significant shift in strategy on Thursday, selling a net $338 million in U.S. stocks. This represents the largest single-day stock sale by retail traders since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic. The action contrasts with the typical investor behavior of purchasing stocks during market declines, known as “buying the dip.” Analysts are currently observing this trend to understand the underlying motivations behind the shift in strategy.

💻 Technology

Dedicated Fans Hire Truck to Protest EA’s Closure of Mass Effect Development •

A group of dedicated fans raised funds to commission a truck displaying the “Save Mass Effect” message and imagery. The vehicle is currently circulating around Electronic Arts’ headquarters in Redwood City, California. The campaign was initiated to advocate for the continued development of BioWare’s Mass Effect franchise following the studio’s closure announced in October. The crowdfunding effort secured funds for billboards and a presence at the December Game Awards. This demonstrates the significant and sustained public interest in the series.

🎭 Entertainment

Melania Launches Controversial Docuseries Amidst Trump’s Political Defeat •

Former First Lady Melania Trump has released a trailer for a two-part docuseries titled “The Series,” just four days after Donald Trump’s significant electoral loss. The documentary reportedly explores the events surrounding Trump’s political campaign and his subsequent defeat. Amazon Studios produced the series, and details about its content remain limited at this time. The release of the trailer marks a notable attempt by Melania Trump to regain public attention following the election results.

🏅 Sports

Jones Faces Backlash After Controversial Comments on Coaching Salaries •

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones issued statements attempting to clarify remarks regarding coaching compensation. Jones previously asserted there was “zero correlation” between coaching salaries and team success. Following widespread criticism, he stated he was open to paying coaches. The comments sparked debate about the financial aspects of NFL coaching contracts and their relationship to on-field performance.

🔬 Science

MAX POWER Aerospace Expo and Airshow Celebrates America’s 250th Anniversary on the Space Coast •

The MAX POWER Aerospace Expo and Airshow is taking place this weekend along Florida’s Space Coast. The event, organized by NASA, commemorates America’s 250th anniversary. It will feature a showcase of next-generation aircraft and spacecraft technologies. The family-friendly event is intended to highlight advancements in aerospace innovation.

🩺 Health

Florida Dengue Fever Cases Surge to 524, Marking Historic Outbreak •

Florida has experienced a significant increase in dengue fever cases, with the state reporting 39 new locally acquired cases within the past week. The disease, often referred to as breakbone fever due to its intense pain, is spreading across the state. Health officials attribute the surge to warmer weather and increased mosquito populations. Currently, a total of 524 cases have been confirmed, representing the largest outbreak in Florida’s history.
